title: Videography Intern
location: In person — Provo, UT + client shoots
summary: Learn to shoot cinematic brand content on real client shoots — composition, light, movement — alongside our videographers.
intro: Peak Exposure Media is a video-first content marketing agency in Provo, Utah. We make cinematic social content for premium brands in home building, design and lifestyle, and we act as the outsourced marketing department for most of our clients. We're looking for a Videography Intern to join our videographers on real client shoots.

This is an unpaid, in-person internship: 5–10 hours a week minimum (more if you want it), any start date, one semester or longer. You'll get full access to our gear and office, a stipend for travel to client locations, and lunch on us at team meetings. If you need it for school credit, we'll sign whatever your program needs.

Here's the honest deal. You'll own one real, recurring piece of client work for the whole semester and get good at it, with our team coaching you along the way. That might be second-camera and B-roll on shoots, running a recurring content day for one client, setting up and breaking down, or shooting behind-the-scenes. You don't need to be great yet. You do need a baseline — this isn't a start-from-zero program — and you need to care about getting better.
We hire for four things: creative bravery, excellence over easy, client obsession and an ownership mentality. Interns too.
processNote: Two steps, both before an interview: a short application and a short written assessment. No test project. We reply to everyone within 24 hours of each step.

values.name: Excellence Over Easy
values.desc: Quality matters; don't rush or choose the easy route.

values.name: Client-Obsessed
values.desc: Care deeply about the client's results, not just completing deliverables.

values.name: Ownership Mentality
values.desc: Act like it's your company, not just a job.

assessment.title: Written Assessment
assessment.blurb: About 20 minutes. Four short questions, 100 words each.

questions.prompt: You walk into a finished kitchen in a custom home at 2pm. Big windows on one side, no lights with you, one camera, one lens. What do you shoot first and how do you make it look good in camera?
questions.strong: Reads the light (where the window is, when to shoot toward vs. with it, exposing for highlights), picks a shot order (wide establishing, then details, then movement), mentions leading lines or symmetry. Red flag: 'I'd fix it in post' or no mention of light.

questions.prompt: Pick any frame from a video or film you love (describe it or link it). Why does it work as a composition?
questions.strong: Talks about where the eye goes and why: placement, depth, negative space, light direction, color, lens choice. Red flag: describes what's happening in the scene instead of the image.

questions.prompt: The builder you're filming is stiff on camera and keeps looking at the lens. You have five minutes. What do you do?
questions.strong: Gets them moving and talking about something they care about, shoots while they're not 'performing', changes the setup (walk-and-talk, over-shoulder, interview with the interviewer off-axis). Shows they'd take care of the client. Red flag: 'tell them to relax.'

questions.prompt: A shot you planned isn't working — the room is too small for the move you wanted. What's your next move, and how do you decide?
questions.strong: Adapts quickly: wider lens, shoot from the doorway, a detail-driven sequence instead of one move, use a mirror or window. Decides based on what the shot needs to say. Red flag: forces the original plan or skips it.

anchors.1: Flat, centered, blown highlights, no intent
anchors.3: Frames are considered; exposure is controlled; understands where the light is
anchors.5: Frames you'd steal — depth, light direction and movement all chosen on purpose

anchors.3: Shoots manual with purpose; footage is clean and stable
anchors.5: Picks frame rate, shutter, profile and lens for the look; could run a second camera on a client shoot tomorrow

anchors.3: Adapts to the room, the light and the subject
anchors.5: Turns constraints into better shots; makes the subject comfortable

anchors.1: No references or 'cinematic' with nothing behind it
anchors.3: Studies specific DPs or brands and names techniques
anchors.5: References match premium home and lifestyle work; restraint over flash

anchors.1: No way to reach shoots, vague availability
anchors.3: Can get to client locations and has set hours
anchors.5: Owns gear, flexible, would show up early

bravery.1: Everything they point to is safe and interchangeable; can't name a creative risk they've taken
bravery.3: Has at least one distinct creative choice they can defend
bravery.5: Clear taste and a point of view already forming; tries things most beginners wouldn't

excellence.1: Shortcuts visible: thin answers, broken links, didn't read the questions
excellence.3: Clean, complete answers; work they share is finished, not half-done
excellence.5: Cares about details nobody asked for; talks about redoing work until it's right

client.1: Only talks about what they want to make; no sense that the work serves a business
client.3: Understands the content exists to get a client a result
client.5: Frames their own ideas around what a client's audience would respond to

ownership.1: Vague goals, blames tools or circumstances, 'tell me what to do'
ownership.3: Specific about what they want to learn; finishes what they start
ownership.5: Already self-teaching, asks good questions, would run a recurring task without being chased

decision.advanceToCall: Skill ≥ 3 with no criterion at 1, every value ≥ 3
decision.hireBar: Shows up reliably and coachable on the call; one recurring shoot or task they can own
